new_entities.name: Orlistat for PCOS
aliases: lipase inhibition for weight loss in PCOS
new_entities.description: Use of orlistat in women with polycystic ovary syndrome, usually in the setting of overweight or obesity, to target metabolic or weight-related outcomes.

new_entities.name: Metabolic outcomes
new_entities.description: Metabolic outcomes such as weight, BMI, waist measures, insulin resistance, glucose markers, lipids, and related cardiometabolic features.

edges.effect_quant: The orlistat-PCOS evidence is mixed rather than cleanly positive. A 2024 guideline-linked meta-analysis found no clear metabolic benefit when orlistat plus a combined oral contraceptive was compared with oral contraceptive therapy alone for fasting insulin, while older randomized and network-meta-analytic evidence suggests orlistat can support weight loss and some androgen or lipid improvements in selected overweight PCOS populations.
edges.population: women with polycystic ovary syndrome, usually overweight or obese and often insulin resistant
edges.mechanism: By reducing intestinal fat absorption and promoting weight loss, orlistat may indirectly improve insulin sensitivity, lipids, and androgen excess, but the net effect depends on comparator, background therapy, and adherence.
edges.summary: This belongs in the mixed bucket. Orlistat can help some anthropometric and metabolic measures, but the benefit is modest and inconsistent across trial designs and treatment combinations.
edges.caveats: Many studies are short, small, or embedded within combination regimens, and the best available meta-analysis found no clear signal for some metabolic endpoints. Tolerability and adherence also affect real-world benefit.

evidence.notes: Anti-obesity pharmacological agents for polycystic ovary syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis to inform the 2023 international evidence-based guideline.

effect_quant.comparator: fasting insulin with orlistat plus combined oral contraceptive versus combined oral contraceptive alone in pooled PCOS trials

evidence.citation: KumarP et al 2011 Reprod Biomed Online
evidence.notes: The effects of metformin or orlistat on obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a prospective randomized open-label study.

effect_quant.comparator: ovulation rate with orlistat versus metformin after 3 months in obese women with PCOS (30% vs 15%)

evidence.notes: Pharmacologic therapy to induce weight loss in women who have obesity/overweight with polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
